results.question: My salary is delayed and my SIP is due soon. What should I check?
results.human_expected: Separates timing from amounts, does not predict a failed debit, and suggests checking balance and dates.
results.rationale: Timing alone does not establish a failed debit.

actual_output.label: AI-generated · passed every quality check
actual_output.summary: Your salary is expected to arrive after the upcoming SIP debit, so the timing of funds may be tight.
actual_output.explanation: The SIP is scheduled for 2026-12-05, while the delayed salary is expected on 2026-12-08, which is 3 days after the SIP date. SIPs are typically processed through a standing instruction or electronic clearing service as described by SEBI and AMFI. If the account lacks sufficient balance for the SIP, the fund house may stop further debits after consecutive missed installments, without a penalty, though your bank could apply its own charges. A salary delay changes only the timing of cash inflow, not the monthly amounts, so the estimated remaining cash remains ₹9,000.00 after accounting for the SIP and expenses.

sources.title: What will the Mutual Funds do, if two or more installments are missed?
sources.locator: Mutual Fund Sahi Hai (AMFI investor education)
sources.excerpt: Electronic debits can be set up through “direct debit” facility or through NACH (National Automated Clearing House). … Just ensure there is sufficient balance in your bank account. … If you miss two or three consecutive instalments, the fund house may stop depositing the post-dated cheques and return all the unused cheques, or stop debiting your account. No penalty is levied and neither is there a forfeiture.
sources.limitations: General description of fund-house practice. It does not cover bank charges, the exact number of failures for a particular scheme, or how a specific mandate is handled.

actual_output.uncertainty: We cannot know the actual balance in your bank account or any bank-specific fees.
